subject: Who owns defense? Proposed owner map + ops SLA for Alden IP claim
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood-inference.com>
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@aldencorp.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed owner map + ops SLA for third-party IP claim (Alden)

Hi Lydia —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per request, attaching a proposed owner map for third-party IP claims tied to the MSA/order form redlines you sent. High-level asks from Alden on notice & evidence timelines look reasonable; we want to be explicit on defense control mechanics so your procurement and legal teams have clear handoffs.

Highlights in this draft: 
- Redwood will accept defense control for claims alleging infringement solely arising from (a) our model outputs when used as intended and (b) our hosted model weights.
- Alden retains the right to take control where customer data or customer-provided code is the primary accused subject.
- Notice + acknowledgement SLA: 3 business days to acknowledge receipt; 10 business days for a substantive response and proposed initial defense plan.

Please see attached defense_owner_matrix.xlsx and Alden_MSA_redlines_v3.docx for inline redline suggestions. If you prefer, we can map owners by claim type (patent vs copyright vs trademark) on the call tomorrow.

Propose a 30-min working session with your legal + procurement to lock final language — are you available Wed 11/22 10am PT?

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber | Strategic Accounts Lead | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: defense_owner_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)]
[Attachment: Alden_MSA_redlines_v3.docx (docx)]

From: Lydia Park <lydia.park@aldencorp.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Alden Procurement <procure@aldencorp.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Nov 2028 10:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Proposed owner map + ops SLA for third-party IP claim (Alden)

Jonas —

Appreciate the quick turn. We reviewed the matrix and have three immediate feedback items: 
1) "Model outputs when used as intended" is a useful starting point, but we need an explicit carve-out for customer-provided prompts containing confidential or proprietary material (we can't rely on "used as intended" alone).
2) We want mutual termination of defense-control if a conflict of interest arises (e.g., Alder legal determines joint defense is untenable).
3) Evidence preservation: we need a 30-day window to request raw logs and will require a preservation hold; please confirm Redwood's ability to produce KV cache slices and request timestamps.

We are available Wed 11/22 10am PT for the working session. I'll loop in our outside counsel if legal adjustments are substantial.

Best,
Lydia Park
Sr. Counsel, Alden Corp
[Attachment: Alden_redlines_comments.pdf (pdf)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood-inference.com>
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@aldencorp.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Nov 2028 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed owner map + ops SLA for third-party IP claim (Alden)

Lydia —

Thanks, that helps. Short answers before the call: 
- Prompt carve-out: we can add a limited carve-out that preserves Alden's right to indemnity for claims tied directly to customer-supplied proprietary content (we'll add a narrow definition and sample indicators).
- Conflict/termination: agree in principle — propose a 7-business-day cure period and workable fallback (split defense costs) instead of unilateral termination.
- Evidence: Redwood can produce request timestamps and platform-level logs on a 30-day preservation hold; for KV cache slices we will provide metadata and an engineered extract (subject to security/e-Discovery process). We'll include an ops contact in the SLA who will triage evidence requests.

Attached is a short compromise clause Kimberly drafted (excerpted) that I want to run by you live.

See you at 10am PT.

Jonas
Jonas Weber | Strategic Accounts Lead | Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com>
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@aldencorp.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Nov 2028 09:35:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Proposed owner map + ops SLA for third-party IP claim (Alden)

Forwarding the excerpted compromise language we discussed. Quoted below is the redline snippet for section 7 (Indemnification & Defense Control):

"7.1 Redwood's Defense Control. Redwood shall have the right to assume and direct the defense of any third-party claim alleging infringement to the extent the claim is based solely on (a) Redwood-hosted model weights or (b) outputs of an unmodified Redwood model when used in accordance with Redwood's published usage guidelines. Redwood shall provide Alden with written notice of assumption within three (3) business days and a proposed defense plan within ten (10) business days.

7.2 Customer-Prompt Carve-Out. Notwithstanding 7.1, Alden shall retain the right to control defense (or require Redwood to cede control) for claims where Alden demonstrates that the asserted infringement arises primarily from Alden-provided prompts, code, or proprietary data ("Customer Materials"). In such cases, parties will engage the cure process in 7.4 and split reasonably incurred defense costs during the cure period.

7.3 Evidence & Preservation. Upon receipt of a valid claim notice, the parties will implement a preservation hold. Redwood will provide platform-level logs, request timestamps, and metadata within ten (10) business days; engineered extracts (e.g., KV cache slices) will be provided subject to security review and with a mutually agreed process and limited scope.

7.4 Cure & Escalation. If a conflict of interest prevents either party from continuing a joint defense, the parties will provide a seven (7) business day cure period to agree on an alternate defense arrangement before any unilateral step is taken. If unresolved, parties will split defense costs pending final allocation by dispute resolution."

This language is intentionally narrow on the customer carve-out and adds clear SLAs for evidence. Happy to tighten wording live.

- Kim
Kimberly Park | Head of Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
